response: Yes, a delay in transfer to a rehabilitation unit can affect outcome after fracture of the proximal femur in older people. Delayed transfer can lead to increased risk of complications, such as pressure sores, deep vein thrombosis, and pneumonia, as well as decreased mobility and functional ability. Additionally, delayed rehabilitation can result in longer hospital stays, increased healthcare costs, and reduced quality of life. Early transfer to a rehabilitation unit can help improve outcomes by promoting early mobilization, reducing the risk of complications, and enhancing functional recovery.
